# Challenges - Missing dependency

When Java is not able to find a class, a
[`NoClassDefFoundError`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/NoClassDefFoundError.html)
is thrown. When using the class path, there is no way for Java to determine
whether all classes are present when the application is starting. This error is
only thrown when the class is not found, and the application will keep working
as long as this part of the code is not executed. This example shows this
problem.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Run the application using Maven

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean compile exec:exec
   ```

   This will work and prints

   ```
   ...
   12:34:56.789 [main] DEBUG demo.Main -- Using a logger
   12:34:56.790 [main] DEBUG demo.Main -- Challenges - Missing dependency
   12:34:56.790 [main] DEBUG demo.Main -- Using Java 25.0.4.1
   ...
   ```

2. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file

   ```
   ./target/libs
   └── challenges-missing-dependency.jar

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the dependencies were copied to the wrong directory

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/wrong-directory'
   ```

   The application dependencies

   ```
   ./target/wrong-directory
   ├── logback-classic-1.6.3.jar
   ├── logback-core-1.6.3.jar
   └── slf4j-api-2.0.18.jar

   1 directory, 3 files
   ```

3. Run the application (**without** dependencies)

   The application uses the logger only when no arguments are provided.
   Consequently, it will fail only in this case, as shown below.

   ```java
   package demo;

   import org.slf4j.Logger;
   import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;

   import java.util.Arrays;

   public final class Main {

       public static void main(final String[] args) {
           if (args.length > 0) {
               System.out.println("Not using a logger");
               System.out.println("Challenges - Missing dependency");
               System.out.println("Using Java " + System.getProperty("java.version"));
               System.out.println("Command line arguments: " + Arrays.toString(args));
           } else {
               /* A logger is used conditionally to demonstrate that missing classes cause a failure only when they are
                   accessed for the first time. */
               final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(Main.class);
               logger.debug("Using a logger");
               logger.debug("Challenges - Missing dependency");
               logger.debug("Using Java {}", System.getProperty("java.version"));
           }
       }
   }
   ```

   Run the application by providing an argument, which will not trigger the
   problem.

   ```shell
   java --class-path './target/libs/*' demo.Main 'No logger!!'
   ```

   Despite the missing dependencies, the application functions correctly because
   the logger classes (`org.slf4j.Logger` and `org.slf4j.LoggerFactory`) are not
   utilised.

   ```
   Not using a logger
   Challenges - Missing dependency
   Using Java 25.0.4.1
   Command line arguments: [No logger!!]
   ```

   Run the application without providing an argument, which will trigger the
   problem.

   ```shell
   java --class-path ''./target/libs/*'' demo.Main
   ```

   The application is missing dependencies. The application starts and only
   fails if a class that it tries to use is not found on the class path or
   module path.

   ```
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: org/slf4j/LoggerFactory
       at demo.Main.main(Main.java:19)
   Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: org.slf4j.LoggerFactory
       at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:580)
       at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:490)
       ... 1 more
   ```

4. List dependencies

   ```shell
   ./mvnw dependency:tree
   ```

   The dependencies defined in the `pom.xml` file

   ```
   ...
   [INFO] demo:challenges-missing-dependency:jar:1.0.0
   [INFO] \- ch.qos.logback:logback-classic:jar:1.6.3:compile
   [INFO]    +- ch.qos.logback:logback-core:jar:1.6.3:compile
   [INFO]    \- org.slf4j:slf4j-api:jar:2.0.18:compile
   ...
   ```

   Our application has the following three dependencies

    - [`logback-classic:1.6.3`](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/ch.qos.logback/logback-classic/1.6.3)
    - [`logback-core:1.6.3`](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/ch.qos.logback/logback-core/1.6.3)
      (transitive)
    - [`slf4j-api:2.0.18`](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/org.slf4j/slf4j-api/2.0.18)
      (transitive)

5. Run the application (**with** dependencies)

   Now that all dependencies are included in the classpath, there is no need to
   provide arguments to use the logger.

   ```shell
   java --class-path './target/libs/*:./target/wrong-directory/*' demo.Main
   ```

   The application works and prints

   ```
   12:35:01.083 [main] DEBUG demo.Main -- Using a logger
   12:35:01.085 [main] DEBUG demo.Main -- Challenges - Missing dependency
   12:35:01.085 [main] DEBUG demo.Main -- Using Java 25.0.4.1
   ```
